historical_reviews.deepseek: Its manual conclusion is correct but does not define what makes either image workable or how to prevent input to the wrong console.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains MANUAL ONLY and adds a bounded operator checklist while separating any driver installation or reboot from KVM acceptance.
historical_reviews.history: No prior exact source identity review exists.
historical_reviews.v3_1: The two views are not independent screenshots: both must show the same verified live SUT while handling concurrent-session/focus behavior. Repeating a harmless marker distinguishes a live second session from a stale copied frame.

original_test_intent: Manually prove that both the embedded and Open-in-new-tab BMC KVM views show the correct live SUT and safely deliver keyboard input in order.
original_method: Verify BMC/SUT identity, browser/KVM compatibility and any pre-approved Aspeed driver state; an operator opens the embedded view, confirms live image changes and enters a unique harmless marker on a designated text surface; then opens the source-defined new-tab view, reconfirms target/session identity and repeats with a different marker while observing focus, duplication, loss, latency and disconnect behavior; finally remove markers and close both sessions.
manual_activity: A human must see the live graphical console, control focus and attest visible responses in both views. Automation may preserve metadata/logs but cannot replace that visual/input judgment.
required_inputs: Approved Aspeed driver package/version and installed-state proof if required
safety_requirements: Confirm target from an independent channel before sending input
Never type credentials, shell commands or destructive key sequences
Use only the designated harmless text field
Stop on stale image, ambiguous focus, duplicated/lost input or target mismatch
Treat driver install or reboot as a separate approved operation
Remove markers and close/orphan-check both KVM sessions
agent_execution_scope: Collect browser, driver and BMC/KVM metadata
Provide the operator checklist and evidence timestamps
Collect BMC session/audit and preserved host logs
Report without claiming visual acceptance or verdict
engineer_actions: Approve driver/browser and safe text surface
Visually verify target and live images in both views
Enter and remove harmless markers while observing focus/input behavior
Close sessions and resolve KVM anomalies

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: No shell command can establish the defining live graphical image and input response, so its non-runnable conclusion is applicable but incomplete.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: MANUAL ONLY: verify the exact target, use unique harmless text markers in the embedded and Open-in-new-tab KVM views, observe freshness/focus/input/latency, capture operator evidence and cleanly close both sessions.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Both KVM views, typing words and 10/10-minute estimates are preserved; driver installation is not silently executed as part of review.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use distinct timestamped markers and one independent target identifier in each view, record visible echo and session behavior, then verify marker cleanup and zero orphaned KVM sessions.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Defines `workable` as same-target live video plus safe ordered input and stable session behavior without replacing human observation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Screenshots or audit logs support attribution but cannot prove live motion, visual correctness or key-to-screen response on their own.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Browser focus or concurrent KVM policy can route, duplicate or suppress input; a stale frame can look correct until a live marker is attempted.

project_override_considerations: The Project must identify whether the Aspeed driver is required on the SUT or client and approve installation/reboot separately. If simultaneous views are disallowed, test them sequentially but still verify the Open-in-new-tab action and session cleanup.
expected_evidence: Verified BMC/SUT, firmware, browser, network and approved driver-state context
Operator-attributed embedded-view capture with target identifier, live-state cue and visible harmless marker
New-tab capture with same target, different live marker and session/tab identity
Focus, input order, duplication/loss, latency, disconnect and recovery observations
Marker removal, both-session closure, BMC/KVM audit plus preserved SEL/OS evidence and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require two BMC KVM views to be usable. Driver details are incomplete prerequisites, not conflicting intent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The target, supported driver/browser and safe surface are normal inputs; the defining operator observation remains clear and feasible.

review_improvement: Turns the vague `workable` criterion into a two-view same-target live-image and input checklist while preventing wrong-console or destructive keystroke hazards.
independent_technical_reasoning: KVM usability is an end-to-end visual interaction: a connection banner or screenshot does not show that the frame is current or that keyboard events reach the intended machine. Distinct harmless markers in each verified view create a causal observation, while focus and concurrent-session checks expose duplication or stale-session defects that a single view would miss.
